Signed-in users may see server-driven security reminders.

Only the scopes a capability needs are requested.

Each message carries an immutable scope enforced at model and tool level.

Each profile resolves its own credentials; unscoped reads fail.
Each message carries the human who sent it so credits and memory go to the sender.

Grouped prompts support all, skip all and don't-ask-again.

Every yes is bound to a fingerprint of the exact request (tool plus canonical JSON arguments, keyed per launch), names the question it answers, is used once, and re-runs through the same gate; a refused or stale yes is spent, and an approved program launch or remote command cannot turn into a different one (serialised arguments, unwrapped wrappers).
Shared safety layer: re-check authority after every await
Owner, profile, App lock, Lockdown and config are re-checked after every await and right before each side effect, using monotonic revisions and run generations, so stale work never acts.
Shared safety layer: caller identity and local-only actions

Each request's caller is resolved once; keys are bound to one conversation and device, risky control changes (Lockdown off, webhooks, people) only come from the local window, the window proves it is talking to the real engine, and viewing sessions and phone-capability lending use one-use, expiring grants bound to owner, profile, device and action.
Shared safety layer: household profile scoping
Household profiles read only allow-listed routes, see and steer only their own tasks, cannot write to owner stores, and get scoped usage and exports.
Shared safety layer: content never grants authority
Forwarded, quoted, copied, exported or persona-written text never changes who is speaking or what is allowed; engine nudges are never treated as the owner's words.
Shared safety layer: secret scrubbing everywhere

Secrets are redacted before truncation, never appear in audit records, URLs, outside-agent messages or unmaskable media, credentials needed in URLs are built and stripped in one place, and problem reports are opt-in, previewed and redacted.
Shared safety layer: no duplicate or replayed side effects

Triggers claim jobs atomically, inbound events are deduplicated before any effect, interrupted work is settled rather than replayed, uncertain sends are reconciled, and only the agent's own delivered messages can be edited.
Shared safety layer: outside-started work is capped
Work started from chat apps, triggers, schedules, voice or paired senders starts no looser than Ask first with a restricted tool list; only the owner's verified direct chat is an exception.
Shared safety layer: chat-app identity and owner authority

A chat account is the owner only when the owner named it; owner commands need a live direct chat, edits count only from the original sender, and an email sender is an identity only with aligned DMARC/SPF/DKIM.
Shared safety layer: automation only narrows permissions
Unattended steps, nested flows, replayed procedures and resumed work get their own capped yes and inherit only the intersection of permissions; per-rule options may tighten but never loosen.
Shared safety layer: settings fail closed and loosening asks

Unreadable settings count as off, damaged key files re-ask, loosening changes (including numeric ones) need explicit confirmation and are refused under Lockdown, model tools cannot reach gateway and update settings, stale proposals are refused, and only one app instance may open a data folder.
Shared safety layer: bounded inputs and honest truncation

Every external read, archive and import is size-, count- and time-bounded and checked before inflating; anything cut off is reported as incomplete; only an explicit 400/413 counts as a context overflow and learned limits only go down.
Shared safety layer: spend caps fail conservative
Incomplete spend totals refuse against the cap, unknown prices stop the next round, and helper model calls use the task's own budget and cancellation.
Shared safety layer: complete deletion and data lifecycle

Deleting removes every derived record through one path, 'delete everything' is all-or-nothing with secure delete, deleted items stay deleted after a backup restore, temporary chats never persist, and backups exclude credentials.
Shared safety layer: screen and browser control

Capture is pinned to the chosen display and excludes the agent's windows, input is bound to the frame the agent saw, ambiguous clicks press nothing, raw CDP is never exposed, and control hand-overs are serialised.
Shared safety layer: update and release identity

Updates are accepted only with proven identity (strict tags, matching versions, exact commit), never downgrade on channel switch, publish only after verification, keep signing keys out of PR code, and only the owner's local window can adopt one.
Shared safety layer: delegated coding agents stay boxed
Delegated coding agents get no shell of their own (a single-job local door instead), no tools for non-owner tasks, and stop if their isolated worktree cannot be proven.
One switch (Settings, mode menu, palette, Ctrl+Shift+L) that makes everything ask, turns off everything that reaches outside, holds on every surface, and shows a banner.
A PIN lock that refuses almost every request while locked, cancels in-flight owner work, rate-limits unlock attempts and needs the current PIN to change.

A Seasons page shows Rings, Gardener and Budding history with measured gains, Veto/Keep/Pin controls, in four languages; Seasons switches (Rings, night window, paid models, min gain) change by asking or in Settings.
Specialist agents are evaluated, promoted and rolled back on evidence.
Ideas drawn from history, a personal feed with an editable prompt, and learning to write like the owner.
